subject: FinTrust VPC mode decision factors + netops sweep
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: FinTrust VPC mode decision factors + netops sweep

Alex / FinTrust netops team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can land on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and what Redwood needs from NetOps if FinTrust prefers Private VPC.

Summary from today's discovery:
- Use case: high-volume document ingestion + PII-sensitive enrichment; compliance requires customer-managed network boundary for production traffic.
- FinTrust preference: Private VPC or Dedicated with private connectivity; leaning to Private VPC for stronger tenancy/isolation.
- Timeline: PoC in 3 weeks, production in ~12 weeks pending procurement.

Key decision factors we discussed (please confirm):
1) Egress/Ingress model — PrivateLink (AWS NLB-based) vs VPC Peering. PrivateLink avoids cross-account route tables but needs endpoint service and static ENI IPs for allowlist. Peering requires route table changes and may be preferred for low-latency internal-only traffic.
2) IP allowlist format — we need a CSV with IPs + CIDR, owner, and purpose. See attached privatenet-ips-template.csv.
3) TLS termination & certs — do you plan to terminate at your edge or will Redwood handle TLS to the endpoint?
4) Network owner & change window — who will own peering/privatelink setup and what maintenance windows exist for route/table changes?
5) NAT/egress responsibilities — clarify who provides outbound internet for model downloads/health checks if using peering.
6) Compliance artifacts — SOC2 report, data retention policy, and audit logs; we can surface Redwood artifacts but confirm if you need them before procurement.

Attachments: MAP-FinTrust-v2.pdf (mutual action plan with milestones), privatenet-ips-template.csv (simple template for allowlist).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Sami or network owner: fill privatenet-ips-template.csv and return by EOD Friday (so our infra team can validate).
- Schedule a 60-minute NetOps workshop (we suggest Thurs or Fri next week) to walk peering vs PrivateLink details and confirm ports/ports ranges. Jordan (cc) to run the workshop.
- I'll update the MAP with concrete network checkpoints and procurement triggers.

If FinTrust opts for Dedicated first, we still need network outlines for egress and possible private routing; differences are mainly around whether you need full tenant isolation (Private) vs reserved infra (Dedicated).

Thanks — happy to tighten the asks if anything above is unclear.

—

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) NetOps contact: looping Sami Rahman (sami.rahman@fintrust.com) who will be the primary engineer on the workshop. Sami — hi, welcome.
2) On PrivateLink vs Peering: our default security posture is PrivateLink for third-party connectivity unless latency requirements force peering. Can you confirm whether Redwood requires any inbound-only ports (i.e., will Redwood initiate connections to our environment or just accept inbound SMB/HTTPS calls)?
3) Static IPs: if PrivateLink is used, do you publish static outbound IPs that we will need to add to our egress firewall? Or do you expect us to open ranges on our side?
4) SLA & artifacts: Procurement will need your SOC2 snapshot and a short note listing data flows (we handle PII storage in a locked bucket). Can you attach both before the workshop?

On the CSV template — we'll have someone fill it out but one ask: can you include a column for "expected traffic direction" (inbound/outbound) and "approx TPS" so NetOps can size NAT/throughput?

Appreciate it — workshop availability: Sami and I are available Thu 09/30 10:00–12:00 PT or Fri 10/01 14:00–16:00 PT. Let me know which works.
